items.X_name: Pitched to the asker's evident level

Score 1.0 when the pitch matches the asker's evident level throughout; 0.5 when there is a local misfit, such as one unglossed term or one over-explained routine point; 0.0 when the pitch is badly mismatched and the very thing the asker lacks is what goes unexplained; NA when the question gives no cue about the asker's level.
items.Y_desc: The answer addresses where the asker actually is: continuing their attempt, confirming or correcting a step they proposed, or resolving the specific confusion the question exposes. items.X_desc: What the answer says it has shown matches what it has shown: a heuristic is called a heuristic, a sketch is not presented as a finished proof, a partial result is not stated as the whole. items.Y_name: Every component of the claim established

items.X_desc: The range over which each claim holds is stated: for which values, on which set, in which regime an identity, inequality, or limit is asserted. items.X_name: Method named with its range of use
items.X_desc: The technique is identified by name or description, and the answer says when it works: the condition under which it applies, or the class of problems it settles. Score 1.0 when the method is named and its range of use is stated; 0.5 when the method is identifiable but transfer is left implicit; 0.0 when the move is presented as a one-off with nothing portable, or with a contentless "this generalizes"; NA when the answer applies no method.
items.Y_desc: External results or sources the answer leans on are named precisely enough to be located, and the answer says what each supplies here. Score 1.0 when every appeal is both identified and given a role; 0.5 when a result is named but its contribution is left for the reader to work out, or the pointer is too loose to locate; 0.0 when a load-bearing fact is imported with no identification at all; NA when the answer appeals to nothing external.

items.X_desc: The answer works on the problem the question poses, not on a neighbouring, easier, or more general one. Score 1.0 when the object of the answer is exactly what was asked; 0.5 when it treats a broader or narrower version and leaves the asked case as an unstated specialization, or spends its effort on adjacent background; 0.0 when it resolves a different problem; NA when the question as titled fixes no determinate problem to target.
items.Y_desc: When the answer proposes a route rather than executing it, the route as described actually arrives at what the question asks for. Score 1.0 when carrying out the stated plan as written would produce the requested object or conclusion; 0.5 when the plan gets part of the way, or needs an unmentioned further idea to close; 0.0 when the plan as stated does not lead to the asked-for result; NA when the answer executes the work itself rather than proposing a route.

items.X_desc: What the answer says it has shown matches what it has shown: a heuristic is called a heuristic, a sketch is not presented as a finished proof, a partial result is not stated as the whole. Score 1.0 when every statement of status is accurate; 0.5 when the answer mildly overstates, presenting a plausible step as settled; 0.0 when it claims to have established something it has not; NA when the answer asserts nothing about its own content, for instance because it only asks the reader questions.
items.Y_name: Hypotheses stated and seen to hold
items.Y_desc: The conditions the argument needs, including the conditions of any result it invokes, are stated, and the answer notes or shows that they hold here. Score 1.0 when the required hypotheses are named and their applicability is addressed; 0.5 when they are named but their applicability is assumed silently; 0.0 when the argument or an invoked result depends on an unstated condition that may fail in this situation; NA when the answer's claims depend on no conditions.

items.X_desc: The answer says what it has concluded, in a form the reader can lift out, instead of stopping at the last manipulation and leaving the inference to be drawn. Score 1.0 when the conclusion is stated explicitly; 0.5 when it is implicit in the final line but never asserted; 0.0 when the answer breaks off with no conclusion and none is recoverable; NA when the answer is by design an opening move that hands the problem back and says so.
items.Y_desc: When the answer proposes a route rather than executing it, the route as described actually arrives at what the question asks for. Score 1.0 when carrying out the stated plan as written would produce the requested object or conclusion; 0.5 when the plan gets part of the way, or needs an unmentioned further idea to close; 0.0 when the plan as stated does not lead to the asked-for result; NA when the answer executes the work itself rather than proposing a route.

items.X_desc: The answer says what it is going to do, and why that route should work, before or as it carries out the moves, instead of opening directly into manipulation. Score 1.0 when a goal or plan is stated and the reader knows where the argument is heading from the outset; 0.5 when an approach is named in passing but the reader must infer the plan from the steps themselves; 0.0 when the answer opens cold and the destination becomes clear only at the end, if at all; NA when the answer makes no argumentative move.
items.Y_desc: Where the answer makes a choice a reader would not reach by default -- an auxiliary quantity, a substitution, a construction, a decision to examine a particular object -- it says why that choice is worth making. Score 1.0 when every such choice carries a stated reason; 0.5 when the main choice is motivated but a further non-obvious one arrives bare; 0.0 when the decisive choice appears with no reason at all; NA when the answer contains no move a competent reader would find unexpected.

items.X_desc: No step the conclusion actually depends on is disposed of by a dismissive phrase -- clearly, obviously, trivially, one checks, it is easy to see -- or by a silent leap. Score 1.0 when dismissive phrasing lands only on genuinely mechanical steps; 0.5 when a non-trivial but secondary step is dismissed; 0.0 when the crux of the argument is disposed of by such a phrase, or skipped without any marker; NA when the answer advances no argument whose steps could be dismissed.
items.Y_desc: What the answer leaves out is left in a state the reader could restore: the omitted step is named -- a theorem, a routine induction, a symmetric case -- rather than merely absent. Score 1.0 when every omission carries a name or pointer sufficient to reconstruct it; 0.5 when an omission is flagged but too vaguely to act on; 0.0 when a step the argument needs is simply missing with no acknowledgement; NA when the answer omits nothing its argument requires.

items.X_desc: The weight of the tools invoked fits what the problem needs: no heavy apparatus wheeled in where a direct argument suffices, and no ad-hoc grind where a standard tool is the natural instrument. Score 1.0 when the tools chosen are the ones the content actually requires; 0.5 when a heavier or more roundabout instrument than necessary is used but still fits; 0.0 when the mismatch obstructs, with machinery burying a simple question or a laborious special-case slog replacing an available standard result; NA when the answer invokes no method.
items.Y_desc: The answer works on the problem the question poses, not on a neighbouring, easier, or more general one. Score 1.0 when the object of the answer is exactly what was asked; 0.5 when it treats a broader or narrower version and leaves the asked case as an unstated specialization, or spends its effort on adjacent background; 0.0 when it resolves a different problem; NA when the question as titled fixes no determinate problem to target.

items.X_desc: Every letter the answer introduces is given a meaning before it is used, and no letter carries two meanings within the same argument. Score 1.0 when every symbol is introduced and stays stable; 0.5 when one symbol appears before its meaning is fixed, or drifts in a way the reader can repair; 0.0 when a reader cannot tell what a symbol denotes, or one letter is silently reused for two different objects; NA when the answer introduces no symbols of its own.
items.Y_desc: The range over which each claim holds is stated: for which values, on which set, in which regime an identity, inequality, or limit is asserted. Score 1.0 when every claim carries the range it needs; 0.5 when the range is given for the main claim but left implicit for a supporting one; 0.0 when a claim is asserted with no indication of where it holds and the reader could not supply it; NA when the answer makes no claim whose truth depends on a range.

items.X_desc: The answer works on the problem the question poses, not on a neighbouring, easier, or more general one. Score 1.0 when the object of the answer is exactly what was asked; 0.5 when it treats a broader or narrower version and leaves the asked case as an unstated specialization, or spends its effort on adjacent background; 0.0 when it resolves a different problem; NA when the question as titled fixes no determinate problem to target.
items.Y_desc: The answer says what it has concluded, in a form the reader can lift out, instead of stopping at the last manipulation and leaving the inference to be drawn. Score 1.0 when the conclusion is stated explicitly; 0.5 when it is implicit in the final line but never asserted; 0.0 when the answer breaks off with no conclusion and none is recoverable; NA when the answer is by design an opening move that hands the problem back and says so.

items.X_desc: Where the answer makes a choice a reader would not reach by default -- an auxiliary quantity, a substitution, a construction, a decision to examine a particular object -- it says why that choice is worth making. Score 1.0 when every such choice carries a stated reason; 0.5 when the main choice is motivated but a further non-obvious one arrives bare; 0.0 when the decisive choice appears with no reason at all; NA when the answer contains no move a competent reader would find unexpected.
items.Y_desc: The answer identifies what makes the problem non-immediate -- the point where the naive approach fails, the condition that is hard to secure -- and its work is aimed there. Score 1.0 when the obstacle is named and addressed; 0.5 when the work implicitly gets past the obstacle without naming it; 0.0 when the answer proceeds as though nothing were in the way and the real difficulty is left untouched; NA when the question poses no difficulty to locate, being a request for a definition or a source.

items.X_desc: What the answer says it has shown matches what it has shown: a heuristic is called a heuristic, a sketch is not presented as a finished proof, a partial result is not stated as the whole. Score 1.0 when every statement of status is accurate; 0.5 when the answer mildly overstates, presenting a plausible step as settled; 0.0 when it claims to have established something it has not; NA when the answer asserts nothing about its own content, for instance because it only asks the reader questions.
items.Y_desc: Where the answer is unsure, the doubt is attached to the particular step or condition in question rather than spread across everything or left out. Score 1.0 when doubt is localized and named, or when nothing is doubtful and the answer commits plainly; 0.5 when hedging is present but unattached, so the reader cannot tell which part is uncertain; 0.0 when contentless hedging pervades, or a genuinely shaky step is asserted flatly; NA when the answer takes no position at all.

items.X_desc: Every part of the answer contributes to reaching the goal: no detours, restatements, or side results the conclusion never uses. Score 1.0 when each part is load-bearing; 0.5 when one identifiable passage is decorative or tangential; 0.0 when substantial portions do not connect to the conclusion at all; NA when the answer draws no conclusion for its parts to serve.
items.Y_desc: The argument runs on a single identifiable idea with the remaining work in its service, rather than several unconnected attempts or a sprawl of cases that never resolves into one reason. Score 1.0 when one mechanism visibly organizes the whole; 0.5 when there is a main idea plus an unintegrated second effort or an avoidable case split; 0.0 when the answer is an assortment of moves with no unifying mechanism; NA when the answer is a single assertion with no structure to organize.

items.X_name: Delivers the requested kind of thing
items.X_desc: The output matches what was requested: a value where a value was asked for, a proof where proof was asked for, a reason where a reason was asked for, and by the means the question stipulates when it stipulates one. Score 1.0 when the deliverable and any stipulated means both match; 0.5 when the right kind of thing arrives by a different route than stipulated, or the request is met only indirectly; 0.0 when a different kind of thing is supplied, for instance a reading pointer where a derivation was requested; NA when the question fixes no deliverable.
items.Y_desc: The answer says what it has concluded, in a form the reader can lift out, instead of stopping at the last manipulation and leaving the inference to be drawn. Score 1.0 when the conclusion is stated explicitly; 0.5 when it is implicit in the final line but never asserted; 0.0 when the answer breaks off with no conclusion and none is recoverable; NA when the answer is by design an opening move that hands the problem back and says so.

anchors.X_desc: Whether the statement the answer finishes on is a true and correct answer to the question that was asked.
anchors.Y_desc: Whether what the answer ends up asserting is actually true for the question posed.

anchors.X_name: Notation is introduced before it is used
anchors.X_desc: Whether every symbol the answer uses is defined at or before its first use.
anchors.Y_desc: Whether the reader is told what each letter stands for before it appears in an expression.

anchors.X_desc: Whether the answer says what makes the problem hard and what its central move exists to defeat.
anchors.Y_desc: How many display-math blocks the answer contains.

anchors.X_desc: Whether the answer verifies that the conditions a cited theorem needs actually hold here.
anchors.Y_desc: How many words the answer runs to.
